findings.issue_text: [BUG] The light-theme branch value was silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness in the small-action a rule. Light-theme users get nearly-washed-out link text where the previous design used scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%); this violates the PR's stated contract of only changing the dark-theme branch.

[BUG] The light-theme branch of .custom-message-length was inverted from $lightness: 70% to $lightness: 30%. Light-theme character-count hint in the modal turns dark and high-contrast, a visible regression that is unrelated to the dark-theme fix the PR claims to make.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the user card .name was changed from 30% to 50% lightness instead of preserving it. Light-theme user names render visibly lighter than before, an unintended visual change outside the PR's stated scope.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the mobile user card .name was changed from 30% to 50% lightness instead of preserving it. Light-theme mobile user names render lighter than before, an unintended regression mirroring the desktop mistake.

[BUG] The light-theme value of the topic list h3 title was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) to 50%. Light-theme topic titles drop from near-full-contrast to mid-gray, a significant readability regression for every mobile light-theme user; the desktop counterpart at topic-post.scss:321 correctly preserves 20%.

[ADVISORY] The adjacent .wmd-input rule still uses darken($primary, 40%) rather than a dark-light-choose/scale-color pair. The disabled composer textarea keeps the legacy darken() color while its sibling #reply-title was converted, so the two disabled inputs diverge visually and the next theming change must be made in two places.

[BUG] The small-action link replacement inverts the intended lightness mirroring: it writes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)) where the original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) and every sibling in this diff uses (N%, 100-N%). In light themes this previously-bold link jumps from 30% lightness to 70% lightness, washing it out against the background; in dark themes it gets scale-color($secondary, 30%), a nearly-black-on-black value instead of the mirrored 70%, making small-action links (reply/like indicators under posts) illegible for dark-scheme users.

[BUG] .custom-message-length swaps the two dark-light-choose branches relative to the original 70% lightness value: it becomes dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), the reverse of the desktop/modal.scss sibling which correctly uses (70%, 30%). On mobile dark themes the character-count hint under the modal textarea renders at 70% lightness of the near-white $secondary — effectively white text where desktop shows 30% — losing the intended secondary/hint styling, and light themes drop from 70% to 30%, making the hint darker than body text.

[BUG] The user-card .name rule replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of the mirrored (30%, 70%). Light-theme user cards lose the 30%-lightness emphasis on names (names render at 50% like ordinary text, no longer visually distinct from .title), and dark-theme names render at only 50% lightness of $secondary where every sibling conversion of a 30% value in this diff uses 70%, producing a washed-out name with poor contrast on dark schemes.

[BUG] The mobile user-card .name rule makes the same non-mirrored substitution as desktop: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) becomes dark-light-choose(50%, 50%) instead of (30%, 70%). Mobile dark-theme user names render at 50% lightness of $secondary (dim, low-contrast versus the 70% used for comparable text), and light themes silently change the name color from 30% to 50%, losing the visual hierarchy between name and title in the user card.

[BUG] The mobile topic title h3 replaces scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) with dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)) instead of the mirrored (20%, 80%) used for the identical desktop h3 in desktop/topic-post.scss line 321. Light-theme mobile topic titles lighten from 20% to 50% lightness, noticeably washing out the most prominent text on the page; dark-theme titles get 50% rather than 80% lightness, so mobile dark-scheme topic titles are markedly dimmer than their desktop counterparts — a visible cross-platform inconsistency for the same theme.

[ADVISORY] The color-scheme conversion hunk sits directly above `.invalid .hex input { background-color: white; }`, a hardcoded white background on the same admin color-picker path that this diff is fixing for dark themes but which the diff leaves untouched. Admins using dark color schemes on the badges/actual color-picker page see a glaring white input box inside the dark-theme `.hex` cells, exactly the dark-theme defect class this PR claims to fix; the next reader will assume this hunk dark-theme-proofed the whole block when it did not.

[BUG] The `.small-action a` color change altered the light-theme branch, not just the dark one: `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` became `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), ...)`, raising the light-theme lightness from 30% to 70%. Light-theme users see small-action links (e.g. post 'edited by' / reply links) in a much dimmer color than before, a visual regression on the unchanged theme that the PR title does not authorize.

[BUG] `.custom-message-length` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`, so the light-theme branch dropped from 70% to 30% instead of being preserved. Light-theme mobile users see the custom message length hint in near-primary-color dark text where it was previously a subtle 70% tint; dark/light branches are also inverted relative to every sibling rule, indicating a copy-paste swap of the two arguments.

[BUG] The user profile `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, altering the light-theme value from 30% to 50% and abandoning the established 100-L mirror pattern (30%/70%). Light-theme desktop user pages show display names in a noticeably lighter gray than before, and the `.name`/`.title` pair no longer has visual hierarchy (both now 50%), degrading contrast the previous CSS deliberately established.

[BUG] The mobile user profile `.name` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, silently changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it per the 100-L mirror convention. Light-theme mobile user pages lose the 30%-vs-50% hierarchy between `.name` and `.title`; both now render identically at 50%, a behavior change on the untouched theme.

[BUG] The small-action `h3` color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`, replacing the light-theme value of 20% with 50% instead of mirroring to 80%. Light-theme mobile post titles inside small-action blocks render significantly lighter than before, and the h3/h4 pair collapses to the same 50% color, removing the intended emphasis hierarchy — a regression on the theme the PR does not claim to touch.

[ADVISORY] Under-scoping: this sweep converted `scale-color($primary, ...)` call sites across compose.scss but left the adjacent `.wmd-input { color: darken($primary, 40%); }` (and the `scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%)` on the neighboring selector) untouched, so the stated invariant — secondary-based colors for dark themes — is not enforced uniformly even within files this diff edits. Dark-theme mobile users still get a primary-darkened composer input color from `darken($primary, 40%)` while surrounding elements were fixed, leaving visible inconsistency in the composer and future maintainers with two competing conventions in one file.

[BUG] The dark-light-choose arguments are swapped: the original light-mode value scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) became the first (light) argument as $lightness: 30%, so the light-theme value changed from 70% to 30% instead of only adding a dark-theme branch. In light themes .custom-message-length changes from a dim 70% gray to a near-full-strength 30% primary color, and in dark themes it renders as a washed-out 70% secondary; the desktop copy (desktop/modal.scss line ~91) still uses 70%/30%, so mobile and desktop diverge on the same component.

[BUG] The light-mode argument was rewritten from the original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) while the secondary argument got 30%, producing the pair (70%, 30%) where the pattern everywhere else is (X, 100-X). Small-action links in the topic post area change color in BOTH themes: light theme goes from 30% (strong text) to 70% (very dim), and dark theme gets 30% secondary (strong) — the visual hierarchy of post-action links inverts instead of being preserved.

[BUG] The original scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%) for h3 was replaced with (50%, 50%) instead of the pattern-conforming (20%, 80%), silently changing the light-theme value from 20% to 50%. Mobile topic h3 titles (a.star block) become half as dark in light themes and lose their boldness contrast, and the desktop counterpart (desktop/topic-post.scss line ~318) keeps 20%/80%, so mobile and desktop headings no longer match.

[ADVISORY] .name was changed from primary 30% to (50%, 50%) in both desktop/user.scss and mobile/user.scss, while the shared rule in common/base/user.scss line ~122 keeps (30%, 70%) for the same .name element, creating three divergent declarations for one visual element. The next maintainer of user-card styling cannot tell which lightness is intended (30 vs 50), and depending on CSS cascade order the common/base value can override or be overridden unpredictably; whoever fixes one copy will miss the others.

[ADVISORY] The diff edits dozens of scattered scale-color($primary, ...) literals rather than introducing a single helper (e.g. a muted-text function/mixin using dark-light-choose with computed complementary lightness), so the (X, 100-X) invariant is hand-maintained at ~50 call sites. Every future lightness tweak must be replicated across all copies; the errors already present in this very diff (swapped 30/70 in mobile/modal.scss, rewritten 30→70 in desktop/topic-post.scss) are direct evidence that hand-maintained pairs drift, and the next editor will repeat them.

[BUG] The review iteration changed the light-theme value in addition to adding the dark branch: the .names a link color's light-theme lightness was silently altered from 30% to 70%. On light themes, the bold username link in the small-action names row goes from a near-primary dark text to a washed-out 70%-lightened text, changing visible light-theme styling beyond the PR's stated intent of only fixing dark themes; this drift was never accepted.

[BUG] The h3 title color's light-theme lightness was silently changed from 20% to 50% while adding the dark-light-choose wrapper. On light themes, the mobile h3 heading loses its darker 20% tone and becomes a 50% mid-gray, altering light-theme contrast and typography hierarchy with no accepted intent for changing light-theme appearance.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length light-theme lightness was flipped from 70% to 30%, the inverse of the desktop/modal.scss counterpart which keeps 70%. On light themes, the mobile custom-message-length hint text darkens from a subtle 70% to a heavy 30% while desktop keeps 70%, breaking desktop/mobile parity and drifting from the accepted 'only change dark themes' objective.

[BUG] The user-card .name light-theme lightness was silently changed from 30% to 50% while wrapping it in dark-light-choose. On light themes, the full-name text in the user summary header loses its darker 30% tone and becomes the same 50% gray as .title, flattening the intended visual distinction between name and title without explicit acceptance.

[BUG] The mobile user-card .name light-theme lightness was silently changed from 30% to 50% while wrapping it in dark-light-choose. On light themes, the mobile full-name text becomes indistinguishable from the .title text (both 50%), eliminating the 30%-vs-50% hierarchy the original design encoded, a silent objective drift beyond the dark-theme fix.

[BUG] The .number, i color's light-theme lightness was kept at 20% but the dark-theme secondary lightness is 80%, inverting the complementary 20/80 pattern used elsewhere only partially — here the light value retains 20% while sibling desktop/topic-post.scss:382 uses the same pairing, but this site's dark value (80% secondary) is light-gray numerals on light backgrounds in dark themes. In dark themes, stats numerals render at 80% lightness of $secondary — a nearly-white tone — where the pattern established by the PR calls for inverse contrast consistent with light theme's dark 20% numerals; dark-theme users get washed-out numbers instead of prominent ones. Rebuttal (dark-light-choose makes it consistent by symmetry) fails because the light theme keeps 20% while dark gets 80%, i.e., emphasis in light becomes de-emphasis in dark, opposite to the PR's 'dim text should stay dim' pattern at matching sites.

[BUG] The dark-theme branch of .embedded-posts a uses scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%) instead of scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%), leaving $primary in the dark slot and violating the PR's own rule that dark themes must derive from $secondary. Dark-theme sites render the embedded-post username in a $primary-derived color (typically near-white on a light background tone) instead of the intended $secondary-derived tone, producing unreadable text in dark color schemes; additionally the light-side value changed from 30% to 70%, altering light-theme appearance even though the PR's stated scope is dark themes only.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length dark-theme argument is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) — $primary instead of $secondary — while the parallel desktop/modal.scss conversion for the same class correctly uses scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%). On mobile dark themes the custom-message-length hint is computed from $primary instead of $secondary, so dark-theme users get a wrongly-colored (typically too-dark/invisible) character-count hint in the flag/message modal, diverging from the desktop behavior for the identical element.

[BUG] The .name rule's dark-light-choose uses identical 50% lightness on both sides and both args collapse toward the same intent, silently changing the light-theme value from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it. User profile names in the topic list become visibly lighter than before on light themes (a regression outside the PR's stated dark-theme scope), and since both branches specify 50% the dark-light-choose adds no dark-theme distinction — a copy-paste that leaves .name effectively un-themed while shipping an unintended light-theme change; the same pattern repeats at mobile/user.scss .name (30% -> 50%/50%).

[BUG] The h3 rule's dark-theme branch uses $secondary at 50% lightness although the light side kept 20%, breaking the complementary inversion (dark side should be ~80%) used everywhere else in this diff. On mobile dark themes the post title h3 renders at 50% $secondary lightness — a mid-gray — while the desktop counterpart h3 (desktop/topic-post.scss line ~318) uses 80%, so the same element has visibly different contrast on mobile dark vs desktop dark, and the h3 loses the strong contrast the old 20% $primary value implied.

[ADVISORY] The whole conversion is a mechanical hand-maintained parallel rewrite — roughly 80 call sites each manually pairing scale-color($primary, N%) with scale-color($secondary, 100-N%) — with no shared helper (e.g. a single mixin like primary-secondary-choose($l)) and no automated check that the pairs stay complementary. The very mistakes already visible in this diff (the $primary-instead-of-$secondary slots in desktop/topic-post.scss and mobile/modal.scss, and the non-complementary 50% values in mobile/topic-post.scss and user.scss .name) are the direct product of this hand-pairing; the next theme tweak touching these files will have to re-edit all sites again and can reintroduce the same silent mispairings, which no test or linter catches because compiled CSS for both schemes is never asserted.

[BUG] The light-theme (first) argument of dark-light-choose for the small-action bold link was changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), unlike every other replacement in this diff which preserves the original light value verbatim. On light themes the small-action link (post dates/reply indicators) becomes 40% lighter than before the diff, rendering near-invisible on light backgrounds for all users; this is a light-theme regression unrelated to the dark-theme fix the PR claims to make.

[BUG] The h3 title color in mobile small-action was rewritten as dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...) instead of preserving the original 20% lightness for the light branch. On light themes the mobile post title drops from a dark 20%-lightness color to a washed-out 50% lightness, degrading readability for all light-theme mobile users — the diff's stated purpose is only to fix dark themes.

[BUG] The .custom-message-length rule was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%)), swapping the original light-theme value of 70% into 30% and also swapping which branch gets which percentage relative to the desktop counterpart it mirrors (desktop/modal.scss keeps 70%/30%). On light themes the custom-message-length hint becomes far darker than before and no longer matches the desktop styling, so the two layouts silently diverge; the arguments appear swapped relative to every sibling rule in this diff.

[BUG] The .name rule's light-theme branch was changed from the original 30% lightness to 50%, deviating from the pattern of preserving the prior light value that the rest of the diff follows. On light themes the user's full name in the profile header loses contrast (30%→50% lightness), a light-theme regression inconsistent with the PR's dark-theme-only intent.

[BUG] The mobile .name rule's light-theme branch was changed from the original 30% lightness to 50%, mirroring the desktop change but still altering light-theme rendering. Mobile light-theme users see the profile header name with reduced contrast compared to the review-base stylesheet — an unintended light-theme behavior change.

[BUG] The light-theme branch was changed from 30% to 70% lightness, inverting the PR's own convention (every other site keeps the $primary branch untouched and adds the $secondary branch at the complementary value). Light-theme users see the action-links username rendered near-white (70% lightness on $primary) instead of the prior dark 30% — near-invisible text on light backgrounds, and dark theme gets the 30% value that belongs on light.

[BUG] The light branch of .staff .name was silently changed from scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) to 50%, and both branches of dark-light-choose are now identical (50%/50%), so the function is a no-op. Desktop light-theme staff names lose their prior darker emphasis and the developer-visible signal that this selector was ever themed is gone — a regression unrelated to the stated dark-theme goal.

[BUG] The light branch of .staff .name was changed from 30% to 50%, making both dark-light-choose arguments identical. Mobile light-theme staff names lose the 30%-lightness color they had before this diff, and the choose call degenerates to a constant.

[BUG] The light branch of a.star h3 was changed from 20% to 50% lightness while the dark branch was also set to 50%, unlike the desktop counterpart (topic-post.scss:318) which correctly keeps 20%/80%. Mobile light-theme topic titles in the star box render at 50% lightness instead of the previous 20%, a visible regression on the light theme and a desktop/mobile divergence for the same component.

[BUG] The light branch of .custom-message-length was changed from 70% to 30% lightness, the inverse of the desktop modal (desktop/modal.scss:94 keeps 70%/30%). Mobile light-theme custom message length text drops from 70% to 30% lightness — dark, heavy text where it was previously muted — and mobile/desktop now disagree for the same UI element.
